newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Balladur says EMU date must be respected.
newsitem.headline: France's Balladur says EMU date must be respected.

text.p: French former prime minister Edouard Balladur, rallying behind the centre-right ahead of a May 25-June 1 snap parliamentary election, said on Wednesday that the calendar for European monetary union must be respected.
"We must follow the calendar that has been set out. It is in our interest to have a single European currency," the Gaullist Balladur said on French television TF1.

Concerning whether or not France, Germany and other European nations might not meet the standards set by the Maastricht treaty for monetary union, Balladur said the treaty was "more flexible than people say. The most important thing is to hold to the date."
Monetary union is scheduled to be launched on January 1, 1999 and the countries participating from the outset are to be chosen early next year.
